sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the scope of judicial discretion during resentencing. The core conflict involves the interpretation of federal sentencing statutes. One side argues for broad judicial flexibility. The other side argues for strict procedural limits. The Court must resolve this statutory tension.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: the side that brought the case wants the Court to allow judges to consider post-sentencing rehabilitation.
The government wants the Court to prohibit judges from considering post-sentencing rehabilitation.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: the side that brought the case argues that categorical bars on variances lack valid legal basis.
The government argues that statutes prevent courts from evading appellate mandates on remand.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This issue determines the practical power of federal judges. It affects how courts weigh rehabilitation in sentencing. It shapes the balance between statutory mandates and judicial discretion. It influences the finality of appellate orders. It impacts the treatment of defendants seeking resentencing.
